title: Kyo Kara MAOH!
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Fifteen-year-old Yuri Shibuya, dunked in a toilet after trying to save a classmate from bullies, is pulled into a medieval-European-style world where he is told he is the Maoh, king of the Mazoku (demons), who live in uneasy peace with humans (MangaUpdates; Bookreporter review). Kind and unwilling to use violence, he must learn to rule on the brink of war, while accidentally ending up engaged to the noble Wolfram. A 21-volume manga adaptation of a light-novel series.
life_message: It holds up justice, kindness and settling conflict without violence, even as a ruler.

content.note: Pirates, a magic duel and war tension (Bookreporter); Yuri rejects violence (MangaUpdates).
Threat of war; light comic tone (review: 'fun and whimsical').
Accidental engagement to Wolfram played lightly (review); BL subtext and male harem (AniList Boys' Love 76%; MangaUpdates); attempted rape listed (to verify).
Light-novel, anime, game and stage franchise (MangaUpdates).

dominant: Pacifist kingship, reconciliation of peoples, humane demons

frames.aligns: Yuri's peacemaking and protection of the bullied echo the common good.
frames.concerns: Demons as a sympathetic people; same-sex engagement as running gag.
Demon king as hero; BL subtext.

frames.aligns: Courage to defend a bullied classmate.
frames.concerns: Demon kingship and magic; male engagement.

frames.aligns: Just rule and restraint of the sword.
Ruler as servant of the people.
Fantasy with a clear moral vision of mercy.
Yuri refuses to solve conflict with violence.

Raja-dharma of a just king; ahimsa.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Yuri refuses violence; a magic duel with Wolfram arises from honor (review).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Court protocol versus Yuri's informal style (MangaUpdates).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Loyalty to the whole kingdom; noble families around him (summaries).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Monarchy and nobles, though Yuri treats people as equals (MangaUpdates).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Customs of the land he must adapt to (MangaUpdates).

folkways.japan: An isekai built on Japanese shoujo conventions, with a schoolboy outsider reforming a rigid court.

delivery.evidence: MangaUpdates summary stresses Yuri's stated ideals; review calls it fun and whimsical, not preachy (to verify).
delivery.note: Subjects who expect a war-leader push back, and the story sides with Yuri.

winners_losers: Yuri's peaceful, humane kingship wins sympathy over the war-ready expectations of his court.
